title: Optimize scenario planner: batching & prefix cache cost model — Opal Insights
summary: Redwood Optimize walkthrough focusing on batching, prefix/KV cache recommendations and a cost-scenario planner tailored to Opal Insights' multi-tenant chat use case. Agreed next steps include a 2-week sandbox with their 2k daily active sessions, security docs and a pricing estimate for a Dedicated pilot.
action_items: Ava Thompson: Share sandbox onboarding guide and console recording; due 2027-12-01
Carlos Mendes: Run quick benchmark recipe for Opal prompt mix and upload results; due 2027-12-06
Priya Shah: Provide sample traffic histogram (session lengths, QPS peaks); due 2027-12-03
next_steps: Schedule 30m sandbox kickoff (Redwood + Opal) — target week of 2027-12-06
Send SOC2 and network architecture docs to Opal security team
Provide pricing estimate for 3-month Dedicated pilot with 2 reserved GPU nodes
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2027-11-29
- Time: 15:00 PST
- Duration: 52 minutes (recording)
- Attendees: Ava Thompson (Redwood AE), Carlos Mendes (Redwood SE), Rita Gomez (Redwood Product), Priya Shah (Opal CTO), Liam Park (Opal SRE), Noah Kim (Opal ML Eng), Sara Blake (Opal PM)

Summary (auto): Quick Optimize demo focused on cost models for Opal's sessionized chat workload; walked through console scenario planner, batch sizing knobs, prefix cache (KV) hit rate assumptions, and suggested pilot configuration. Customer asked about data residency, KMS, and how fallbacks work if cache miss spikes.

00:00:08 Ava: Hey everyone faint hello, thanks for carving time. I'm Ava from Redwood, AE for Opal, and I'll hand over to Carlos to walk through the Optimize scenario planner.
00:00:18 Carlos: Hey Priya, Liam, Noah — good to meet you, uh quickly i'll share my screen. The thing i want to emphasize up front is we're going to model three lanes: hosted fast path, dedicated reserved, and private/VPC — but given your compliance notes we'll focus dedicated/VPC economics.
00:00:40 Priya: Sounds good, we care about predictability and cost at scale. our primary worry is latency spikes when customer sessions warm up, and token billouts.
00:00:55 Carlos: Exactly — so first slide is workload profile. Noah you sent your session distribution right? small chat 1-3 turns common, 1.8k daily active sessions, but tail of long sessions to 2k tokens.
00:01:12 Noah: Yes i uploaded a sample histogram, but note the older data has some logging issues so there might be noise in the >5k bucket.
00:01:22 Ava: no worries that's why we run sandbox runs. quick Q — do you expect lot of concurrency or more session-affinity?
00:01:30 Liam: session affinity, we pin users to a session id for context so many concurrent sessions but usually a single inflight request per session. bursts around product launches.
00:01:40 Carlos: perfect, that pattern maps well to prefix (KV) cache wins — the demo will show cost delta moving from zero cache to 40%/60% hit scenarios.

00:02:12 [screen share starts]
00:02:17 Carlos: ok console, Optimize -> "Scenario Planner". The planner lets you plug in model latency profiles, token costs, and caching hit rates. I'll start with your baseline: 1.3k avg tokens per session, 1.8k sessions/day, 200 peak QPS is an input. Here's the default batch window and concurrency slider.
00:02:41 Sara: Can you call out the batch window meaning? is that an SDK param or runtime tunable?
00:02:47 Carlos: It's runtime tunable; our serving runtime accumulates small requests into continuous batches up to latency SLO. The slider simulates effective batching without changing client code. In production we auto-balance to meet latency targets.
00:03:05 Priya: and that batching only affects cost right, doesn't change semantics?
00:03:10 Carlos: Correct — it doesn't modify outputs. only inference packing — although in extreme cases var batch sizes can change tail latency, which is why we let you pick latency SLO and simulate.

00:03:36 Carlos: Now prefix cache — here's the KV cache pane. You can model a per-session prefix length (how many tokens kept warm) and expected hit rate. I'll demo three scenarios: no cache, conservative 30% hit, and aggressive 60% hit.
00:03:50 Liam: What drives hit rate in practice? is it shared prompt templates or user-specific context?
00:03:56 Carlos: both — repeated system messages, prompt templates, and common user intents raise hit rate. For Opal with templated system prompts and repeated QA pairs, we expect a nice middle ground around 35-45% with some prefetch strategies.
00:04:12 Priya: prefetch? we don't want to blow up tokens if we prefetch too much.
00:04:18 Carlos: totally. prefetch in Redwood is workload-aware — you can set lookahead depth and max prefetch tokens per session. The planner shows incremental token overhead vs hit benefit so you can see net savings.

00:04:49 [00:04:50] Carlos: Switching to the cost modeling table. baseline hosted per-token cost, dedicated instance cost per node (monthly), and an input for KV cost (we charge small persistent mem usage + lookup cost). In this example a 40% KV hit reduces per-session token consumption by ~28% after accounting prefetch overhead.
00:05:12 Priya: how do you account for KV storage when sessions are long? do we pay for long-term KV per user?
00:05:19 Carlos: KV is TTL'd by session; recommended pattern is session-scoped caches for chat. for longer retention you can move to pinned session stores but that increases storage cost — the planner has a storage cost toggle.
00:05:31 Noah: curious about how batching interacts with KV hits — if a request is served from KV, does it still benefit from batching?
00:05:38 Carlos: cached responses avoid some expensive decode steps but still may go through light-weight shaping, so you see some CPU but much lower GPU time. Batching primarily helps uncached requests; we model combined effects in the planner.

00:06:02 [00:06:05] Carlos: Let's run the scenario: baseline (no cache, modest batching 8ms window) — estimated monthly tokens 120M, GPU hours 420, monthly infra $34,200. Now toggle KV to 40% hit with conservative prefetch: tokens down to 86M, GPU hours 300, infra $24,800. Net monthly delta ~27% savings.
00:06:36 Priya: nice, those numbers help. can you show sensitivity to cache hit rate?
00:06:42 Carlos: yep — here's the sensitivity curve. small changes near 0-20% don't move needle much; the biggest marginal returns occur 30-50%. above 70% you plateau unless you optimize prefetch aggressively.

00:07:05 Sara: one operational concern — what if a mass invalidation happens (e.g., system prompt change)? do we have an automated invalidation across nodes?
00:07:12 Carlos: yes we support atomic policy invalidations and TTL shading. The runtime coordinates via control plane to flush or rekey caches; we'll also coordinate safe rollouts to avoid cache stampedes.

00:07:42 [00:07:45] Carlos: next is batch sizing. in the planner you can simulate different concurrency targets: lower concurrency (small batches) favors latency but costs more; higher concurrency pushes throughput up, cost per token down but tail latency increases. For Opal, given session-affinity, a medium concurrency (16-32) balances well.
00:08:07 Liam: can Redwood suggest an autoscale policy for bursts? like threshold-based on queue depth?
00:08:12 Carlos: We have pre-built autoscaling policies — queue depth, 95th-latency, or token backlog. For your launch spikes, we recommend queue-depth + burst pool that can spin up 2 nodes for 10-minute windows.
00:08:28 Priya: what's the SLA during a burst if we consume reserved capacity?
00:08:33 Carlos: Reserved Dedicated nodes are under SLA; burst pool may be on shared capacity depending on commit. We'll document exact fallthrough in the pilot proposal.

00:08:55 [screen: console trace view]
00:08:58 Carlos: here's a trace example — you can see token timing, kernel time, cache lookup time annotated. there's also a cost-per-token column; this helps you attribute hot prompts.
00:09:11 Noah: do we get per-prompt quality metrics? like if batching changes generation nondeterministically?
00:09:17 Rita: We track evals tied to prompt sets. batching is deterministic in our runtime, but variations in generation stem from model sampling; for critical prompts we recommend locked seeds or smaller temperature for deterministic outputs.

00:09:40 [00:09:43] Sara: security: how is KV encrypted at rest? can we use our KMS?
00:09:48 Carlos: For Private and Dedicated, you can bring your KMS (AWS KMS / Cloud HSM) and we support envelope encryption. For hosted we encrypt with our managed keys but can enable customer-managed keys for certain tiers.
00:10:02 Priya: audit logs and RBAC — can we map to internal SSO groups?
00:10:07 Ava: yes SAML/SCIM provisioning supported, and audit logs include per-request metadata. we'll get your security team the SOC2 and architecture doc after this call.

00:10:30 [00:10:33] Carlos: back to the planner: i want to demo the "what-if" slider — change prefetch depth from 16 tokens to 64 tokens per session, see token overhead and net savings. When prefetch is aggressive, hit rate increases but prefetch tokens become overhead for less-likely flows. The planner shows net savings matrix.
00:10:58 Priya: can this be automated? like Redwood Optimize suggests a prefetch depth based on observed hit curve?
00:11:04 Carlos: yes that's part of the Optimize recommendations — our engine will propose warm-up lengths and max prefetch tokens based on your observed session heatmaps, with safe guardrails. We surfaced a recommended profile on the right.

00:11:30 [00:11:32] Carlos: Let's sketch a pilot config: two Dedicated GPU nodes (n1 with 8 A100-equivalent gpus each) for baseline throughput, plus a 1-node burst pool. We'll enable session-scoped KV with 48-hour TTL, and Optimize's dynamic prefetch with conservative profile. Expected monthly infra $28k with projected 22-28% savings vs hosted.
00:12:00 Priya: that price looks reasonable — one ask, can you show how fallbacks work if KV lookup rate increases beyond provisioned limits?
00:12:08 Carlos: fallback is automatic: misses route to a compatible model variant or node tier. The control plane will throttle prefetch and temporarily widen batching window to reduce pressure. You can set a strict fallback policy like 'never degrade below X latency' which pins to higher-cost nodes.

00:12:35 Liam: a bit worried about cache storms if many sessions rewarm after an outage — do you have guardrails?
00:12:41 Carlos: we do — adaptive rewarm pacing, circuit-breaker per-session, and coordinated rebuild strategies. We can simulate rewarm storms in the sandbox to tune behavior.

00:13:02 [00:13:05] Carlos: Now i'll run a live simulation — I'll upload your sample histogram and we'll replay 48 hours compressed into 5 minutes to see cost and hit-rate changes under burst conditions.
00:13:18 [audio: typing, upload noise]
00:13:40 Carlos: ok starting sim now — timeline bar at top, watch the infra cost delta panel.
00:13:48 [00:14:02] Priya: interesting the hit-rate dips during the midday spike, why is that?
00:14:07 Carlos: because many new sessions start simultaneously so cold-starts increase; prefetch amortization per session is lower. That's why we recommend a small warm pool pre-warmed for launch periods to keep hit rates stable.
00:14:25 Noah: how big would the warm pool be for a 30% uplift in morning peak?
00:14:30 Carlos: in your case, about 0.2 nodes — practically i'd propose a 1-node warm pool that we scale down outside windows. The planner shows warm-pool ROI.

00:14:55 [00:15:00] Sara: product question — can the console surface per-customer tenant cost if we go multi-tenant?
00:15:05 Carlos: yes per-route and per-API-key cost breakdown is built-in. You can map session ids to tenants and run chargeback.

00:15:20 [00:15:25] Priya: what telemetry do we need to send to get good suggestions?
00:15:29 Carlos: sample traffic histogram (session length, tokens per request, inter-arrival), and prompt fingerprinting (hashed) for hot-prompt detection. We don't store PII — we only store hashed prompt signatures for analytics.
00:15:45 Priya: good. we'll need an NDA addendum for hashed fingerprint processing.
00:15:50 Ava: we can add that to the security packet.

00:16:05 [00:16:08] Carlos: quick note on model selection: the planner lets you pick model variants and quantization profiles. For Opal we'd recommend a 7B quantized variant for most flows and a larger 13B for long-form sessions where quality matters. You can route by policy.
00:16:28 Noah: route by policy — can we do A/B between model variants to measure quality vs cost?
00:16:32 Carlos: absolutely — canary and A/B rollouts are first-class. The console shows per-variant metrics and regen-rate differences.

00:16:50 [00:16:53] Sara: if we pilot Dedicated, what's expected infra provisioning lead time?
00:16:58 Ava: typically 2-3 weeks for Dedicated node provisioning in our regions, faster if you can accept shared node burst or in certain cloud partners. We'll coordinate timelines in the SOW.

00:17:20 [00:17:25] Carlos: last live demo bit — I'll save the scenario as "Opal-prod-conservative" and export the CSV. This contains the detailed per-day token projections, node hours, and KV storage estimate.
00:17:40 Priya: can you share the CSV after the call?
00:17:43 Ava: yes will attach in follow-up.

00:17:55 [00:18:00] Customer Q&A (rapid fire)
00:18:02 Liam: what about data residency in eu-west? we have customers there.
00:18:06 Ava: we have region pins and for Dedicated/Private you can choose region; we'll include EU region pricing.
00:18:14 Sara: licensing concerns for tokens generated that contain customer content?
00:18:19 Rita: Standard contract language applies; we'll have legal signoff and can add special terms if needed.
00:18:25 Priya: can we limit retention for ephemeral sessions?
00:18:29 Carlos: yes per-route retention and TTL controls.

00:18:45 [00:18:48] Carlos: quick note about cost allocation — the Console supports tagging routes and breaking down token/unit costs, also a simulation mode for hypothetical changes (e.g., drop prefetch to zero for certain tenants).
00:19:05 Noah: would be helpful to run per-tenant simulations — some tenants are heavy and deserve different policies.
00:19:11 Carlos: we can run multi-tenant scenario runs in the sandbox.

00:19:32 [00:19:35] Priya: ok last question — what's the expected P50/P95 latency with the conservative setup you proposed?
00:19:41 Carlos: P50 ~ 120ms for most prompts on Dedicated 7B quant variant, P95 ~ 380ms with current batching policy; with more aggressive batching you can reduce cost but P95 increases.
00:19:57 Priya: that's within our target, P95 target 400ms so good.

00:20:10 [00:20:13] Ava: Recap — we'll share: 1) sandbox onboarding + console recording, 2) CSV export and pricing estimate, 3) SOC2 & security docs. Customer to share traffic histogram and any legal constraints. Agree pilot window next week?
00:20:27 Priya: yes target week of 12/6 works.
00:20:32 Sara: i'll get calendar invite and share internal stakeholders.

00:20:45 [wrap-up chatter]
00:20:50 Noah: small nit — in your console the prefetch toggle looked like it was on by default; will it change outputs for existing routes?
00:20:56 Carlos: no changes without explicit rollout; Optimize suggestions are proposals you must accept.
00:21:05 Priya: thanks all, this was super helpful.
00:21:09 Ava: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and attachments.

[Transcript ended at 00:21:15 but recording shows full 52 minutes due to Q&A and follow-ups; omitted longer side conversations to keep transcript focused. Additional logs and console export attached in follow-up email: link to CSV (internal), security packet (link), sandbox invite (link).]
